workflowRecommendation: Strictly sequential on one branch (legion/LEGSMOKE-143) and one pull request into main: implementer (file + push + PR) -> tester (acceptance 1-3 at its head, E2E line) -> reviewer round 1 (COMMENT; head still carries .legion/) -> implementer pushes the .legion/ deletion -> reviewer round 2 (APPROVE naming the clean head by SHA; acceptance 4) -> retro by the revived implementer (one docs/solutions/ commit + Dispatch message) -> merger (threads, --summary checks, READY to notifications.role.pr-queue) -> merge queue squash-merges -> implementer verifies on main and records it on the PR and the issue (acceptance 5) -> architect re-runs the acceptance-5 commands, sets the issue done, reads it back (acceptance 6). The repository has no build, test suite, linter, formatter, AGENTS.md, or repository-local skills; every proof is a command against GitHub or Dispatch whose output is recorded.

implement: legion-worker — supplies the path-limited `jj split`, the `bookmark set -r @- --allow-backwards` push, the PR body READY format with the `Dispatch: LEGSMOKE-143` line, the re-run-not-repush CI rule, rebase only on CONFLICTING, the .legion/ deletion push, and the post-merge production check.
legion-retro — the same implementer is revived after the APPROVE for the mandatory retro: one docs/solutions/ commit above the approved head, one Dispatch message with the retro footer, no handoff.
dispatch — the retro message and the post-merge record go on the Dispatch issue with dispatch_message in plain English, because `legion gh` refuses every GitHub-issue write.
test: legion-worker — defines the E2E section the tester writes (real surface, exact commands, observation, head SHA, one negative control, links) and the handoff write/split/push gate.
verification-before-completion — each acceptance line is proven by running its named command and recording the output; the implementer's handoff is never the evidence.
review: legion-worker — one review per round via `legion gh -- api --method POST repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/pulls/<n>/reviews` with commit_id; COMMENT while .legion/ is on the head, APPROVE only the clean head named by SHA; CI, threads, and E2E verified on GitHub, never from a handoff; Thermo line omitted on this docs-only PR.

concerns: The working-copy commit @ carries the daemon-provisioned empty .omp/config.yml (jj `snapshot.auto-track = all()`; the repository has no .gitignore). It must never reach GitHub. `jj split -m <msg> <paths>` leaves the bookmark on the REMAINDER commit (the new @, undescribed, holding .omp/config.yml), and `jj git push` refuses an undescribed commit. Every phase therefore runs `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" bookmark set legion/LEGSMOKE-143 -r @- --allow-backwards` before `jj git push --bookmark legion/LEGSMOKE-143`; without --allow-backwards jj refuses to move the bookmark from @ to its parent. The planner observed both behaviours in this workspace while committing plan.json (see plannerObservations).
Anything written under $LEGION_WORKSPACE is auto-snapshotted into @. Scratch files (PR body, review JSON, expected-bytes file, negative-control directory) live under /tmp, never in the workspace.

The planner committed .legion/plan.json locally and advanced the local bookmark legion/LEGSMOKE-143 to that commit but did NOT push, on the architect's instruction ('Do not push a branch or open a pull request; the implementer does that'). The implementer's first push publishes the plan commit, the smoke-file commit, and the implement handoff together.

Both workflows run on `push` AND `pull_request`, so every head shows FOUR check-runs (job `check` x2 from workflow `ci`, job `gate` x2 from workflow `fail-on-demand`), observed on PR #43 head 69d8dd375f81. `gh pr checks` prints job names; `gh run list --branch legion/LEGSMOKE-143 --limit 50 --json databaseId,name,event,conclusion,headSha` prints the workflow names the spec uses (`ci`, `fail-on-demand`). Use --limit 50: the default 20 can drop older heads' runs. The `ci` job sleeps 20 s; wait with `legion gh -- pr checks <n> --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --watch` before reading conclusions. A red run is re-run with `legion gh -- run rerun <run-id> --failed`, never by pushing.

Byte comparison: `cmp - <(printf …)` fails on this machine (cmp cannot seek a process substitution). Write the expected literal to /tmp/legsmoke-143-expected.md with change.createCommand's printf and run `… | base64 -d | cmp - /tmp/legsmoke-143-expected.md; echo exit=$?` (verified: identical -> silent exit 0).
Thermo: the PR is a single 96-byte markdown file (docs-only), so per legion-worker the reviewer runs no thermonuclear pass and omits the Thermo line entirely.

Sibling LEGSMOKE branches with open PRs (#32 LEGSMOKE-104, #41 LEGSMOKE-132, #42 LEGSMOKE-131, #43 LEGSMOKE-137) add different smoke/ files and may merge first. A newer main is NOT a rebase trigger; only GitHub `mergeable: CONFLICTING` is. The one path that could collide is retro's docs/solutions/ file: its filename must contain `legsmoke-143` so no sibling retro produces the same path.

The merge queue squash-merges: PR #38 and #33 merge commits on main each have exactly one parent. Acceptance 5's squash proof is `parents|length == 1` AND the merge commit's parent does NOT contain the smoke file (a rebase-merge's tip parent would already contain it; a merge commit would have two parents).
`legion gh` refuses GitHub-issue writes; legion-retro's message and the post-merge record are Dispatch writes (dispatch_message on LEGSMOKE-143).

After the .legion/ deletion push nothing writes a handoff: cleanup, APPROVE, retro, merger READY, and the post-merge confirmation report with `legion handoff complete` alone. Recreating .legion/ changes the approved head and restarts the review loop.

All phases commit as legion-implementer[bot] (jj user.email observed in this planner pane) and PR #43's three body edits are all attributed to legion-implementer, so the tester's `pr edit` is expected to work. Fallback if `pr edit` returns HTTP 403: post the filled E2E line as a PR comment with the Legion footer and tell the architect so the implementer pastes it into the body on its next push.

Acceptance 2 names the retro learning under docs/solutions/ as part of the final diff; the reviewer's APPROVE at the clean head sees only the smoke file (retro runs after approval), the merger and the architect see smoke file + one docs/solutions/ file. No scope tension.

rebasePolicy.onlyTrigger: legion gh -- pr view "$N" --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus reports mergeable CONFLICTING (or the controller asks because of a conflict). A newer main, a red or flaky CI run, or wanting fresh CI is never a trigger (Sami, 2026-09-11). With a unique smoke filename and a legsmoke-143 retro slug this branch cannot conflict with the open sibling branches.
rebasePolicy.fingerprint: cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" git fetch && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" diff --from "fork_point(main@origin | <head-sha>)" --to <head-sha> --git --context 0 '~(.legion | docs/solutions)' | sed -e '/^@@/d' -e '/^index /d' | sha256sum
procedure: Record the fingerprint at the current tip (the bookmark's commit, @-).
cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" git fetch && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" rebase -s 'roots(main@origin..@)' -d main@origin
Record the fingerprint at the new tip.

legion gh -- pr comment "$N" --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --body $'rebase <old-tip-sha> → <new-tip-sha>; fingerprint <before> → <after>; unchanged|changed\n\n<!-- legion: {"session":"<session-id>","phase":"implement"} -->'

unchanged -> confirmation only: the tester re-checks the bare gates (four check-runs success at the new head) and edits the E2E head SHA with 'rebase re-check <old> → <new>: fingerprint unchanged, bare gates only'; a prior APPROVE gets one confirming APPROVE naming both SHAs. changed -> full test round and one new review.

ciFailurePolicy: A failed check-run at any head: read it with `legion gh -- run view <run-id> --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --log-failed`. Flaky or infrastructure failure -> `legion gh -- run rerun <run-id> --failed`, never a new commit. Real failure caused by this change (only possible if `.fail-me` reached the tree, which allowedPaths forbids) -> fix in this PR. `ci` cannot fail on content (it only sleeps 20 s and exits 0).
